proof: If a semisimple 3x3 matrix A is Sym^2 B over a field of characteristic 0, its eigenvalues with multiplicity are alpha^2, alpha*beta, beta^2. Hence det A=(det B)^3 and one eigenvalue alpha*beta=det B has cube equal det A. Our A has det1 and none of 4,8,1/32 has cube1, so it is not Sym^2 B even over an algebraic closure. Yet reduction mod7 is exactly chi^2,1,chi^-2 for chi(g)=2 mod7. Thus the residual triple does NOT alone imply arbitrary characteristic-0 deformations are symmetric squares of GL2.
limitation: This is only a single matrix over Q_7 with the right residue, not a full global Galois representation or polarized deformation. It rules out a naive functorial inference, not a sophisticated compatible-family argument.
